When the write protection bit of a parameter is set to 0, it means that this parameter is not write-protected and can be programmed.
Setting the write protection bit of a parameter to 1 enables write-protection for it and none of its bits can be modified afterwards.
Non-programmed bits always remain 0 while programmed bits always remain 1.
